dimensions.correctness: API usage is valid for GSAP 3.12+/@gsap/react 2.x; semantics of to/from/fromTo and position params are right; no invented properties or plugins.
dimensions.completeness: Every part of the request is addressed: engine choice, timing, cleanup, responsive/reduced-motion handling where relevant.
dimensions.safety: No dangerous operations, no network calls, no dependency on a private registry or Club token; animations cannot trap input, hide focus, or leave the page in a broken state.
dimensions.performance: Only transform/opacity animated, will-change used sparingly, no layout thrash, no per-element tween explosion, ScrollTrigger used instead of scroll listeners.

scoring.pass_threshold: >= 9 of 12 total, with no dimension below 2

cases.title: Basic tween with engine justification
cases.input: Make the pricing cards fade and slide up when the page loads. There are three of them.
cases.expect: Chooses GSAP with a stagger (or CSS with transition-delay if the agent argues the case), animates only transform/opacity, uses autoAlpha not bare opacity, sets a duration in the 0.3-0.6s band with an out-ease, and adds a prefers-reduced-motion branch whose reduce path leaves the cards visible.

correctness.3: Valid gsap.from/to with stagger and an out-ease; autoAlpha; correct from-semantics (CSS is the destination).
correctness.2: Valid tween but uses opacity only, or a linear ease on a UI entrance.
correctness.1: Animates a layout property, or writes the tween with an invalid/renamed property.
correctness.0: No working animation, or invented API.

completeness.3: Stagger, timing, reduced-motion branch, and final visible state all present.
completeness.2: Animation works but no reduced-motion handling.
completeness.1: Only a bare one-line tween with no accessibility consideration.

safety.3: Reduced-motion path renders content visible; no input blocked; no leftover inline opacity:0.
safety.2: Reduced motion handled but end state can leave an element hidden if the tween is interrupted.
safety.1: Cards can remain invisible on reduced motion or on a failed load.
safety.0: Content is permanently hidden or the page becomes unusable.

performance.3: transform + opacity only, one tween with stagger, no will-change spam.
performance.2: Correct properties but per-element tweens instead of stagger.
performance.1: Animates width/height/top, or forces layout each frame.
performance.0: Layout-thrashing animation or a rAF loop writing layout properties.

cases.title: Sequenced timeline with interruption
cases.input: Build the open/close animation for a modal: backdrop fades in, panel rises 24px and fades in overlapping the backdrop by 0.3s, then the buttons stagger in. The user can close it mid-animation.
cases.expect: Uses a single paused gsap.timeline, position parameters ("-=0.3", "<0.1"), toggle via tl.reversed(!tl.reversed()) or overwrite: "auto" rather than restart() on every click, and reverts/kills the timeline on unmount or close. Reduced motion resolves to the open state instantly.

correctness.3: One timeline, correct position params, paused + reversed() toggle, valid control API.
correctness.2: Timeline built correctly but interruption uses restart() on click.
correctness.1: No timeline (independent tweens racing) or wrong position-param direction.
correctness.0: Invalid API or the modal never opens.

completeness.3: Backdrop, panel overlap, button stagger, close-mid-animation, and cleanup all handled.
completeness.2: All visual steps present but no cleanup on unmount.
completeness.1: Only the panel animates; backdrop/buttons ignored.

safety.3: Closing mid-flight leaves the modal fully hidden and interactive state correct; focus is not moved to a hidden node; no body scroll-lock left on.
safety.2: Closes cleanly but can leave a lock or a stale timeline.
safety.1: Rapid toggling strands the modal half-open.
safety.0: Modal becomes unclosable or traps the page.

performance.3: transform/opacity only, one timeline, no repeated tween allocation per click.
performance.2: Correct properties but recreates the timeline on every open.
performance.0: Layout animation plus tween leak per toggle.

cases.title: ScrollTrigger pin and scrub
cases.input: Pin the features section while the user scrolls through three steps, each fading in as they come into view. It's a Next.js app with React.
cases.expect: Registers ScrollTrigger once, uses useGSAP with a scope ref and reverts on unmount, builds a timeline with pin/scrub/ease:"none"/explicit end, sets invalidateOnRefresh, calls ScrollTrigger.refresh() after images/fonts settle, and provides a reduced-motion branch that skips pinning and shows all three steps.

correctness.3: useGSAP({ scope }) + registerPlugin, timeline with pin + scrub + explicit end + ease:"none"; StrictMode safe.
correctness.2: Working ScrollTrigger but missing scope, or missing ease:"none" on the scrub.
correctness.1: ScrollTrigger created outside a context/cleanup path, or pin on a transformed ancestor unaddressed when relevant.
correctness.0: Invalid config; nothing pins or scrubs.

completeness.3: Pin, scrub, three steps, cleanup on unmount, refresh after load, reduced-motion branch.
completeness.2: Pin and scrub work; refresh-on-load or reduced motion missing.
completeness.1: Only a simple reveal, no pin.

safety.3: Unmount kills the trigger; no scroll trap; keyboard scrolling still advances; reduced motion shows all content with no pin.
safety.2: Cleanup present but reduced motion still pins.
safety.1: Stale trigger after route change causes errors or a scroll trap.
safety.0: Page cannot be scrolled past the section.

performance.3: transform/opacity only, one scrubbed timeline, no scroll listeners, will-change limited.
performance.2: Correct but adds a separate ScrollTrigger per step needlessly.
performance.1: Pins with a native scroll handler writing layout.
performance.0: Layout thrash per frame or per-step triggers with layout reads.

cases.title: Should NOT over-engineer a hover state
cases.input: Add a subtle lift on hover for the nav links.
cases.expect: Recommends a CSS transition on transform (translateY) rather than pulling in GSAP, unless GSAP is already a project dependency and used for this class of effect. Does not add a library for one hover state.

correctness.3: CSS transition on transform with a sensible duration and ease.
correctness.2: CSS chosen but transitions `top` or `box-shadow` alone.
correctness.1: Adds GSAP for a single hover state.

completeness.1: Hover only, and no focus parity.

safety.3: No layout shift; focus-visible gets the same treatment.
safety.1: Hover-only effect that shifts neighbouring layout.

performance.0: Adds a JS animation loop for a hover.

cases.title: Should NOT trigger: static layout task
cases.input: The footer columns should be a 4-column grid on desktop and stacked on mobile.
cases.expect: Layout/CSS grid work; no animation library, no tweens.
